draft.title: Activity levels and trends
card: Surveys collect data on how many Australians meet the physical activity guidelines. In most age groups, fewer than half of people meet them.
Activity changes with age. Children are the most active, and activity usually falls through the teenage years and into adulthood.
Many teenagers fall well short of the 60 minutes a day that the guidelines set for young people.
Sedentary behaviour, such as sitting for work, study and screen time, has been rising over time. A trend is the direction a measure moves over time, so this is a rising trend.
draft.remember: Most people miss the guidelines, activity falls with age, and sitting time is rising.

a.q: A national survey finds that activity usually drops between childhood and the late teens. What does this show?
opts: Activity levels change with age
Activity levels stay the same with age
Teenagers are more active than children
Only adults are affected by inactivity
a.why: Data that shows a drop from childhood to the late teens shows that activity changes with age. It does not say teenagers are more active, because the data shows the opposite.
a.clue: Compare the age groups in the data, not one group alone.

b.q: A survey in Bendigo finds that 35% of 15-year-olds meet the guidelines, and the share of time they spend sitting has risen over ten years. Which conclusion fits this data?
opts: Most of this age group miss the guidelines and sit more
Most of this age group meet the guidelines and sit more
Most of this age group miss the guidelines and sit less
Most of this age group meet the guidelines and sit less
b.why: Only 35% meet the guidelines, so most do not. Sitting time has risen, so they sit more. The option saying most meet the guidelines misreads 35% as a majority.
b.clue: Is 35% more or less than half?

b.best: Most of this age group miss the guidelines and sit more

problems.detail: The stem already says activity drops between childhood and the late teens, so 'Activity levels change with age' just restates it. The other options plainly contradict the stem or are absurd, which makes this too easy for Year 11 and does not test reading of trend data.

a.q: A Geelong survey finds 60% of 5 to 8 year olds, 40% of 9 to 12 year olds and 20% of 15 to 17 year olds meet the guidelines. Which conclusion fits?
opts: Fewer people meet the guidelines at older ages
More people meet the guidelines at older ages
Most 15 to 17 year olds meet the guidelines
The share meeting the guidelines stays steady with age
a.why: The share falls from 60% to 40% to 20% as age rises, so fewer people meet the guidelines at older ages. Only 20% of 15 to 17 year olds meet them, so most do not.
a.clue: Read the numbers from the youngest group to the oldest.
